R552.note: HTML-escapes the Referer value and swaps the format() sink for write(), closing both the XSS and the format-string vector; the switch away from format() is stated plainly and no legitimate caller depended on the format expansion.

R553.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 and UTF-8 on both interpolated fields; nothing else changed.

R554.note: Build FAIL (CS0246 on UnknownIdentifierException, wrong namespace for DynamicExpresso), so the fix does not compile; it also swaps in a new third-party dependency and adds a character allowlist that rejects previously-accepted formulas (commas, string literals, comparisons) and throws instead of returning a value.

R555.note: subprocess.run with an argument list and shell=False plus a fullmatch on the format the docstring already documents (short alphanumeric report key); verified in a scratch dir that Python's list form still launches a .bat on Windows (rc 0), so the function keeps working and the returncode/RuntimeError path is preserved.

R556.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES,'UTF-8') on the POST note and on the two GET echoes; the added null-coalesce on $_POST['note'] is stated in the write-up and blocks nothing.

R557.note: CR/LF and '>' rejection closes the RCPT injection, but the added strict email regex is a new restriction the original did not have and rejects RFC-valid addresses (e.g. an apostrophe or other atext specials in the local part), turning them into an IllegalArgumentException.

R558.note: Binds RS256 via new Key($publicKey,'RS256') so the token's alg header cannot select the algorithm; the 6.x upgrade is stated, and no legitimate token verified under the old call since $hmacSecret was never passed to decode - minor: the exception named in the prose is UnexpectedValueException, which the existing catch already covers, and the '7.1.0 current' aside is unsourced.

R559.note: escapeshellarg on $host is the right PHP API for this sink and nothing else changes; residual gap only that a quoted leading '-' is still read by ping as an option, which the write-up does not mention.

R560.note: RFC 4515 hex escaping with the backslash replaced first, applied where the filter is built; only unstated side effect is that a missing username now yields '(uid=)' rather than '(uid=undefined)', which matches nothing either way.

R561.note: Minimal UPLOAD_ERR_OK guard placed before the finfo probe and the move, matching the finding exactly with no other change.

R562.note: payloadLength > frameBuffer.size() guard before the memcpy, returning false and leaving lastPayloadSize_ untouched on rejection; explanation's talk of 'subtracting smaller from larger' is stray prose, no subtraction exists.

R563.note: Canonical it = tasks.erase(it) / else ++it loop; removes every completed task, keeps order, skips nothing.

R564.note: UPLOAD_ERR_OK check is the fix; the extra fileinfo guard and the MIME-derived filename extension are disclosed, block no legitimate upload, and nothing consumes the stored name - though the extension change is scope creep justified by a rationale that does not apply (the client filename was never used).

R565.note: Detail moved to log.Printf and a generic body returned with the same 500 status; only the intended response-body change.

R566.note: Server-side IsInRole("Admin") gate runs before DeleteAccountAsync and before isDeleting is set, so only unauthorized invocations change behaviour; the cascading Task<AuthenticationState> parameter is the shape Microsoft recommends over injecting AuthenticationStateProvider, and an unhandled UnauthorizedAccessException tears down a Blazor Server circuit rather than rendering a message.

R567.note: execFile with shell:false cannot launch a .bat on Windows - reproduced in a scratch dir on Node v24.3.0: it throws 'spawn EINVAL' synchronously, so the callback never runs and the route's own 500 handler is bypassed; injection is closed only because the script can never execute, and the write-up asserts the opposite ('receives reportName as %1, no escaping necessary').
